title: Madjedbebe rock shelter
summary: A sandstone rock shelter on Mirarr Country at the edge of Kakadu in northern Australia. Excavations dated by luminescence suggest people first used it about 65,000 years ago, give or take 5,000, making it Australia's earliest documented site, though the age has been debated.

uncertainty.note: ABC News (reporting the 2017 Nature study) says all dating pointed to about 65,000 years, give or take 5,000. An earlier excavation suggested up to 60,000 years and was disputed.

where.modern_name: Madjedbebe (Malakunanja II) rock shelter, Arnhem Land / Kakadu region, Northern Territory, Australia
where.historical_name: Mirarr Country; no polity at this date

importance.justification: Its dating bears directly on when people reached Australia and on the timing of dispersal out of Africa.

reviewer_note: The Nature paper (Clarkson et al. 2017) would not open, so the age rests on ABC and UQ summaries. The 65,000 figure is contested by some researchers per search snippets I did not open; the ABC page notes the earlier up-to-60,000 estimate was disputed. GeoNames places it in Arnhem Land.
